Subject: Thanks for the demo — a couple of follow-ups

Ava — thanks for the concise demo today. High level we liked the latency numbers and the ability to route to a cheaper quantized variant for lower-priority requests. Two follow-ups from our eng team while we finalize the pilot: 

1) SDK/auth — we need an implementation sketch for token exchange + short-lived API keys so we can map requests to internal accounts. Do you support automatic token rotation or do we need to run a proxy?

2) Structured output reliability — we need a clear validation + retry recommendation for the JSON responses. Our product needs a guaranteed-safe schema (orders/transactions) and we’d rather failover than return malformed JSON.

3) Embeddings + reranker — what are warmup/embedding caching expectations? Can the reranker hit an embedding service or should it be colocated?

Also attaching the recording you promised and a short one-pager with our pilot objectives. Can you send a brief mutual action plan with owners and dates?

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Finlytics

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — a couple of follow-ups

Jordan — appreciate the clear asks, and great questions. Short answers up front:
- SDK/auth: we support both API-key rotation and mutual TLS for Private deployments; hosted uses short-lived bearer tokens with automatic rotation via our Control Plane. We can provide an SDK example that shows token refresh and service-account mapping.
- Structured output: we recommend a two-layer strategy (runtime constrained decoding + post-response JSON schema validation + deterministic retry on validation failure). See details below.
- Embeddings/reranker: recommend colocating reranker with embedding cache for latency-sensitive queries; we support in-process caching in the SDK for warm prefixes.

Action items:
- @dev_patel — can you sketch the SDK auth flow and an example config (token refresh + header signing) and drop the snippet in-thread? Due EOD tomorrow.
- @neha_kapoor — I’ll need a 1P mutual-action plan with dates; can you own the timeline and customer comms?

I’ve pasted a compact technical checklist here to keep alignment. I’ll follow up with a Drive link to the proposed mutual action plan.

---
Runtime JSON safety checklist (summary)
1) Constrained decoding: model-level stop sequences + token-biasing for structural anchors when generating JSON arrays/objects.
2) Response post-check: schema validation (fast AJV-style checks) before surface to product.
3) Retry policy: on schema failure, attempt up to 2 autoregressive fixes (prompted retry with stricter decoding constraints), then fallback to a simpler template-based renderer.
4) Observability: log raw + validated outputs, and tag samples that triggered retry for quality review.

Will iterate on the snippet once @dev_patel posts it.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — SDK auth + snippet (technical)

Looping in the technical sketch and an SDK example. Short technical notes first:

- Auth flow we recommend for hosted pilot:
  * Client obtains short-lived client token from Redwood Control Plane via OIDC client credentials (recommended: 1h TTL).
  * SDK transparently exchanges refresh token + rotates local token before expiry.
  * Request header: Authorization: Bearer <token>; include X-Org-ID for routing to dedicated pools.

- SDK config (node/python pseudocode):
  * token_refresh: true
  * cache: {embedding: {ttl_seconds: 3600}, prefix_kv: true}
  * routing: {latency_slo_ms: 200, cost_priority: balanced}

- Structured output handling:
  1) Response comes back as streaming token chunks. SDK applies a \"structural-anchor\" bias on characters like '{', '\"', ':', ']' for first 512 tokens to favor valid JSON tokens.
  2) SDK attempts local parse; if parse fails, it sends a constrained-rewrite prompt (include the original response frozen + explicit schema) to the same model with higher temperature clamp and a max token budget of 120.
  3) If rewrite fails JSON validation twice, SDK falls back to a deterministic template where we map best-effort fields and set a \"validation_status\":\"partial\" flag.

- Retry pattern rationale: we want to avoid black-box retries that resubmit the whole user prompt; instead use targeted constrained-rewrites so cost is bounded.

I attached a tiny snippet file with a pseudocode example for the token refresh header and the constrained-rewrite flow (sdk-auth-snippet.txt).

Let me know if you want the snippet converted to an open-source gist or sample repo.

— Dev
Staff Engineer, Runtime

Subject: Mutual action plan & timeline (pilot prep)

Jordan — thanks for the pointed questions. Per our internal alignment, here’s a short mutual action plan and owners so we can hit pilot kickoff the week of Sep 14.

Mutual action plan (summary)
- Sep 2: Redwood provides test harness + constrained-decoding checklist (owner: Dev Patel) — deliverable: runbook + small dockerized harness you can run against your prompt set.
- Sep 4: Trial credentials + example SDK token rotation repo (owner: Ava Chen) — deliverable: repo link + quickstart README.
- Sep 7: Embedding cache recommendations for serverless (owner: Dev Patel) — deliverable: config options + warmup scripts.
- Sep 9: Joint run of synthetic validation (owner: Finlytics: Jordan; Redwood: Dev) — deliverable: 7-day synthetic run results.
- Sep 11: Pilot kickoff prep call (owner: Neha Kapoor) — deliverable: mutual-action-plan.xlsx and meeting agenda.

Notes:
- SLO mapping: constrained-rewrite p50 ~ 120ms on our preferred model; p95 ~ 650ms when a rewrite is required (this is measured on dedicated pools; hosted numbers will be similar but vary by region). We will include these numbers in the runbook.
- Embedding cache: SDK provides a per-instance LRU cache by default; for serverless we recommend a hot-warm strategy (short TTL + pre-warm endpoint) or a shared redis cache for low-latency hot items.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Next steps: I’ll drop the Drive link to the mutual-action-plan and create a short calendar invite for Sep 11. If this timeline looks good, reply with a quick ACK and any calendar conflicts.
